2. CCN(CC)CC - This is triethylamine (Et3N), which is a tertiary amine. Tertiary amines are typically very weak acids with pKa values around 40-50 (they're actually bases, with conjugate acids having pKa values around 10-11).

3. SC1=CC=C([N+]([O-])=O)C=C1 - This is p-nitrothiophenol, which contains a thiol group (-SH) and a nitro group. The nitro group increases the acidity of the thiol, giving it a pKa typically around 4-5.

Ordering from most acidic (lowest pKa) to least acidic (highest pKa):
1. p-toluenesulfonic acid (pKa ≈ -1 to 0)
2. p-nitrothiophenol (pKa ≈ 4-5)
3. triethylamine (pKa ≈ 40-50)
